scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Dhemsa is an ancient tribal folk dance of the Desia, Gond, and broader Adivasi peoples in southern Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, and the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra, India.

In urban contexts, organizations like Kosodum Welfare Private Limited, Gondwana Jangom Dhemsa Rela Nrutya Dal, and Gondwana MitraMandal have organized performances of Gond Tribe artists in Mumbai to promote and preserve the tradition.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dhemsa is generally performed late at night during annual community ceremonies including Chait Parab and Pus Puni (also referred to as Pus Parab).
It serves as a major social and ritual group performance during these annual festivals.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by traditional folk instruments: the dhol drum, the tamak' drum, the changu drum, and the mahuri wind instrument.
The musician playing the mahuri is known as the Mohuria, and the drummers follow the lead of the Mohuria.
Listen for the dhol, tamak', changu, mahuri.
The music features high-register melodic phrases from the mahuri wind instrument played by the Mohuria, anchored by steady, repetitive tribal drumming on the dhol, tamak', and changu.
